maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0095-002

Asset: WELL-0095 (SW-24 Well 095, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 06 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 06 Jan 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 15 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0095-0012 on 2023-01-05 Report written: 06 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0095-0012 at 15:15 on 2023-01-05 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.0% of the pad area, estimated 3.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level; one crew member's monitor had not been bump-tested that day (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 325 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 260 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0095-002 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.5% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Notes and recommendations

maintenance.action: Fished and replaced parted rod section
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0095-008

Asset: WELL-0095 (SW-24 Well 095, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 05 Jan 2024 08:00 · Finished: 10 Jan 2024 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 132 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0095-0062 on 2024-01-04 Report written: 11 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0095-0062 showed the wellhead at 9.4 °C with the air at 6.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 4 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Rod couplings1,620

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0095-012

Asset: WELL-0095 (SW-24 Well 095, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 23 Jun 2024 08:00 · Finished: 26 Jun 2024 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 75 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0095-0085 on 2024-06-20 Report written: 27 Jun 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0095-0085 showed the wellhead at 34.4 °C with the air at 35.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly1,577
Bolts, shims and seals394
Bearing grease and consumables657
Labour (company crew)1,389
Total4,017

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0095-021

Asset: WELL-0095 (SW-24 Well 095, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 19 Dec 2025 08:00 · Finished: 13 Jan 2026 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 600 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0095-0163 on 2025-12-18 Report written: 19 Jan 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0095-0163 showed the wellhead at 15.2 °C with the air at 8.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.
